title: Integration value playbook + security cheatsheet
author: Aisha Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips sales engineers and partner teams with a compact, actionable set of positioning statements, technical talking points, pilot pricing templates, and a short security FAQ tailored to integration partners and platform alliances. It is designed to shorten cycles for ISV integrations, marketplace listings, and embedded deployments where buyers demand predictable economics and clear risk controls.

Scope: merchant platform integrations, SaaS ISV partners, channel embed deals, and private deployments where the partner owns the customer-facing UX.

Owners and cadence
- Document owner: Aisha Chen (Go-to-Market, Field Enablement)
- Technical reviewer: Mateo Ruiz (Solutions Engineering)
- Security reviewer: Priya Nair (Security & Compliance)
- Review cadence: quarterly or post-major-product-release

Positioning & 30-second value scripts
- For platform leaders evaluating embedded models:
  - Quick pitch (business): "Ship generative features that scale — predictable latency, lower cost-per-call through batching/caching, and enterprise controls for data residency — without building your own serving stack."
  - Quick pitch (technical): "Single API, model pinning, and canary rollouts with automated fallback to lighter quantized variants means you get deterministic latency and consistent throughput across hosted, dedicated, and private modes."

Competitive snapshot (how to frame common pushbacks)
- Competitor: Managed cloud AI endpoints (C1)
  - Angle: "one-stop" simplicity.
  - Redwood counter: Operational levers (batching, KV cache, quantization profiles) deliver 20–45% unit-cost reductions for bursty workloads; show a simple cost calc during demos.
- Competitor: Self-hosted inference runtimes (C2)
  - Angle: Total control.
  - Redwood counter: We provide VPC/on‑prem private deployments plus a control plane and audited rollout tooling — avoids multi-quarter infra projects while retaining governance.
- Competitor: LLM APIs with opaque performance (C3)
  - Angle: Fast and cheap at small scale.
  - Redwood counter: Highlight SLOs and observability: per-route latency percentiles, token-level cost breakdowns, and regression alerting tied to prompt sets.

Positioning evidence to bring to calls
1) Deterministic latency: 99th percentile targets per offering (sample):
   - Hosted API: 99p < 150ms (short completions, <512 tokens)
   - Dedicated: 99p < 120ms (pinned GPU pools, configured batching)
   - Private (VPC): SLA-driven by contract (typical target 99p < 200ms)
2) Cost delta examples (ballpark, for discussion only):
   - Chat UI (interactive): Redwood batching + prefix caching -> 25–40% lower $/interaction vs naive single-request endpoints
   - High-throughput embed inference: Dedicated quantized variants -> 40–60% lower $/vector than large fp32 deployments
3) Reliability: multi-variant fallback keeps traffic live during model or region outages.

Pilot & pricing playbook (three standard pilot offers)
- Pilot A: Developer POC (14 days)
  - What: Hosted API, up to 100k tokens, single model, access to Console dashboards
  - Pricing: Free credits + $0 for first month of usage; overages billed at hosted rate with cap
  - Success criteria: integrated call in product UI, smoke test of throughput, 95% of test prompts pass quality gate
- Pilot B: Production pilot (30–90 days)
  - What: Dedicated capacity reservation (small), model pinning, canary rollout tools, SLO monitoring, onboarding support (SE + Solutions Architect)
  - Pricing: Commitment-based discount (negotiated); typical structure: monthly commit + usage overage at discounted unit price
  - Success criteria: latency within SLO 95p, cost per active user under agreed target, operational runbook accepted
- Pilot C: Private proof (VPC)
  - What: Private control plane + customer-managed compute / on-prem package for regulated data
  - Pricing: Professional services + platform license (term-based), security review lead time (2–6 weeks)
  - Success criteria: compliance checklist met, audit evidence reviewed, successful production traffic switch-over test

Pilot pricing quick-calculator (example table)
| Pilot tier | Typical commit | Onboarding time | SE hours included | Common buyer 
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------|--------
| Dev POC   | $0–$1k credit  | 2 weeks         | 4 hours            | Developer/team lead
| Production| $5k–$25k /mo   | 2–4 weeks       | 20 hours           | Platform eng + infra
| Private   | $50k+ /term    | 4–12 weeks      | 40–80 hours        | Security + IT

(Use the table values as negotiation starters; always align to legal / commercial)

Demo checklist (technical win conditions)
1. Console walkthrough: per-route latency chart, token cost waterfall, and model catalog.
2. Live integration: embed a quick chat or summarization call from partner UI showing 95p latency.
3. Failure mode demo: simulate model variant failure and show automatic fallback to lighter quantized variant.
4. Security brief: show KMS integration, audit log sample, and tenant isolation model.

Sample rebuttals and scripts
- If prospect says "we host everything ourselves": 
  - Script: "We respect that. Redwood is designed to be flexible — Private deployments let you keep compute and keys; our value is the hardened control plane and rollout/observability stack that prevents regressions and shrinks time-to-safe-feature-launch."
- If prospect asks about cost predictability:
  - Script: "We recommend commit-based Dedicated for predictable throughput, combined with token ceilings and console alerts to prevent surprise bills. We can model expected $/active-user during the pilot."

Short case study vignette (one-page summary for field use)
- Customer: Fintech B2B ledger provider (anonymized)
- Problem: inconsistent latency on peak batch scoring and inability to roll back model regressions safely
- Redwood solution: Dedicated pool with smart batching, canary rollouts, and regression alerts tied to prompt set captures
- Result: 34% drop in $/inference, 2x improvement in peak throughput, and zero customer-facing regressions during 6-month rollout

Technical appendix (snippets to share in an integration repo)
- Sample REST call (hosted):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1", "input":"Summarize product feedback for Q1."}'

- Example minimal policy for canary rollout (YAML):
  rollout:
    strategy: canary
    canary_percent: 10
    metric: latency_99p
    thresholds:
      - step: 1
        max_latency_ms: 200
      - step: 2
        max_latency_ms: 250

Security & risk cheatsheet (top 10 buyer questions with short answers)
1. Where is my data stored?
   - Answer: By default hosted data is stored in Redwood regions; for regulated workloads we provide VPC/private deployments and can support customer-managed storage.
2. Do you log prompts / outputs?
   - Answer: Audit logging is configurable. For private deployments, logs remain inside the customer VPC. Hosted logs can be redacted on ingest and subject to retention policy.
3. How are encryption keys managed?
   - Answer: KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM) are supported; keys can be customer-controlled in private deployments.
4. Can we run in an air-gapped environment?
   - Answer: Yes — we offer an on-prem package; expect a 6–12 week delivery timeline for full air-gapped validation.
5. How do you prevent model regression leakage?
   - Answer: Rollouts are bound to prompt-set evals and regression alerts. We support automatic rollback and test harness gating.
6. What certifications do you have?
   - Answer: SOC 2 Type II (hosted), ISO 27001 in progress; specific compliance packages available for enterprise.
7. What access controls exist?
   - Answer: RBAC in Console, per-token credentials, and audit trails.
8. How do you handle data residency requests?
   - Answer: Region pinning and private deployments ensure data stays in customer-chosen geography.
9. What is the incident process?
   - Answer: Standard incident response with customer notification SLA in enterprise contracts; runbooks and postmortems shared on request.
10. How do you guarantee uptime during model upgrades?
   - Answer: Canary and multi-variant routing with automated fallback to compatible quantized variants maintain availability during upgrades.

Security artifacts to offer during evaluation (checklist)
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
- Network architecture diagram for VPC/private deployment
- Sample audit log extract and retention policy
- Data processing agreement template
- Pen test summary and remediation log

Operational handoff checklist (before production cutover)
1. Confirm SLOs and alert thresholds with platform team.
2. Finalize model pin and canary policy.
3. Exchange KMS/HSM details and key rotation plan.
4. Schedule runbook handover session (Ops + SE).
5. Agree on billing/commit terms and overage caps.
